## What These Are For

Sometimes you know what you want from an AI tool but struggle to figure out how to say it. These sentence starters are short, flexible phrases you can drop into a prompt to make it more specific, clearer, or more useful.

Mix and match. You don't need all of them — pick the ones that fit your situation.

## Setting the Goal

Use these to open a prompt with a clear statement of what you're trying to accomplish.

- *"My goal is to…"*
- *"I am trying to build / write / understand / fix…"*
- *"I need help creating…"*
- *"I want to end up with…"*
- *"The end result I'm looking for is…"*

## Adding Context

Use these to give the AI the background it needs to help you well.

- *"I am working on a project that…"*
- *"This is for [class / assignment / personal project] where…"*
- *"I'm at the point in my project where…"*
- *"What I've done so far is…"*
- *"The relevant part of my code / essay / draft is…"*
- *"Here is what already exists that this needs to connect to:…"*

## Naming the User or Audience

Use these when the output needs to fit a specific reader or user.

- *"The user for this is…"*
- *"My audience is…"*
- *"I'm writing this for someone who…"*
- *"This needs to be accessible to someone who has never…"*
- *"The reader already knows…, but does not know…"*

## Setting Constraints

Use these to define what the output should and shouldn't include.

- *"Please use only…"*
- *"Do not use…"*
- *"Keep the response to…"*
- *"Format the output as…"*
- *"Only address…, not…"*
- *"Avoid…"*
- *"I haven't learned [concept / library / syntax] yet, so please don't use it."*

## Asking for Reasoning

Use these to get the AI to explain its thinking, not just give you the answer.

- *"Please explain your reasoning by…"*
- *"Walk me through your thinking step by step."*
- *"After giving the answer, explain why you approached it this way."*
- *"If there are multiple ways to do this, explain which you chose and why."*
- *"I want to understand this, not just use it — so please…"*

## Naming Assumptions and Limits

Use these to flag things the AI should not assume or to acknowledge uncertainty.

- *"Avoid assuming…"*
- *"Do not assume I have access to…"*
- *"I'm not sure whether…, so please flag if that affects your answer."*
- *"If my setup is unusual, let me know."*
- *"If there are constraints I haven't named that matter, point them out."*

## Pointing Out Tradeoffs

Use these when you want the AI to surface options and their consequences, not just give you one answer.

- *"If there are tradeoffs, point them out."*
- *"If there's more than one reasonable approach, describe them briefly before recommending one."*
- *"Flag any risks or edge cases I should be aware of."*
- *"Let me know if this approach has downsides I should weigh."*

## Steering a Follow-Up

Use these when you're continuing a conversation and want to adjust or build on the previous response.

- *"The part I'm not satisfied with is…"*
- *"The [first paragraph / second function / third bullet] needs to…"*
- *"This is close, but can you adjust [specific thing] so that…"*
- *"Keep everything else, but change…"*
- *"Building on what you just gave me, now…"*
- *"Can you explain [specific part] in more detail?"*

## Asking for Help Understanding

Use these when you've received output you need to understand better before using it.

- *"Can you walk me through this line by line?"*
- *"Can you trace what happens to [this input] step by step?"*
- *"I understand [part], but I'm not following [other part] — can you explain just that?"*
- *"What would happen if I changed [this] to [that]?"*
- *"In plain language, what is this actually doing?"*
name: 2. Sentence Starters
